analysis.title: GS Coppersmith - US EQUITIES the flight to quality 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: SPX is within 1% of all-time highs while the median S&P stock is 16% below its own high. GS's preferred breadth measure is at its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble.
The GS Quality factor has rallied more than 16% over the past 8 weeks, the largest move since the COVID shock in 2020. The desk reads this as more risk aversion beneath the surface than SPX suggests.
The desk does not view narrow market breadth as a warning sign and favors SPX higher over the next 1-3 months.

Bloomberg studied 13 episodes since 1995 where the 10 largest S&P stocks outperformed equal weight by more than 8% over three months. The median subsequent SPX return was +10.1% over 6 months and +19.6% over 12 months, versus historical medians of +6.9% and +15%. The current gap is 855bps.

Positioning is light. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at -1.3, a level where forward returns look more attractive. Global fundamental L/S net leverage is in the 6th percentile over the past year (2nd percentile for the US) and overall HF net leverage is in the 10th percentile, while gross exposures remain elevated.

Fundamental L/S funds lost 70bps between October 2-8, driven by negative alpha on both longs and shorts. US single stocks were net sold for a third consecutive week, with short sales outpacing long buys.

Tech flows reversed sharply. After being the most net bought sector in four of the prior five weeks, Tech was by far the most net sold last week through long sales and incremental shorting. Tech L/S ratio is 1.8 (17th percentile over five years) while gross allocations remain in the 97th percentile.

Industrials saw their fastest pace of buying since January (+1.8 SD), almost entirely new longs after five consecutive weeks of selling. The L/S ratio is in the 22nd percentile over five years. Financials also saw buying and Software showed relative strength.

Staples was net sold in seven of the past eight weeks, entirely through shorting, pushing its L/S ratio to the 3rd percentile over five years. Biotech had its largest cumulative eight-week percentage de-grossing in more than five years. The desk says neither is necessarily a buy signal.

After the move above 5% in 10-year yields, the GS Rates team sees asymmetry skewed toward lower yields, and rates vol has started to reverse. The desk says equities need stability rather than a large Treasury rally.

The GS Commodities team expects Brent to moderate toward $90 by December and average $80 in 2027, but sees risks skewed meaningfully higher near term. More than $20/bbl of risk premium is embedded in prices. Oil is the biggest threat to a more constructive rates and equity backdrop.
NVDA is offering downside implied volatility at levels not seen since before Covid. The desk sees this as an opportunity to hedge against an unwind in the AI trade or crowding in quality.

The desk's overall view is that earnings are supportive, positioning is light, and extreme concentration alone is not a reason to turn bearish. Absent another move higher in both oil and rates, the path of least resistance is higher.
